answer: A farm cannot share one proof across a hundred names, so its costs multiply while its reward stays single. A name without Recorded bridge keeper fair token is turned away at the counter, and a token keepers wear after bridge inspections is the reason the counter can tell. Cheap to join once, ruinous to join a hundred times — that is the point. The toll is a 30-day stay in the queue, with no way to buy a shorter one per entry, collected at the gate with no refunds for ghosts. The voyage is checked, not assumed. The clerk notes yarrow. One lotus, one entry.
